ana: Heads-up — we're getting a couple reports about the JS SDK behaving differently across runtimes: Node (undici) vs edge (global fetch) vs bundlers. Also some TS consumers hitting weird types when using CJS wrappers. Anyone seen this today?

sam: seeing it. Two quick categories: runtime detection/fallbacks for `fetch`, and ESM/CJS interop for our exported helpers (types + default export shape).

mike: can you paste a minimal repro? I want to know if it's an import/runtime error or runtime missing APIs.

ana: (typo) I meant @ana :)

ana: repro from a user in Cloudflare Workers:

```js
// worker.js
import { RedwoodClient } from 'redwood-sdk'

addEventListener('fetch', event => {
  const c = new RedwoodClient({ apiKey: SECRET })
  event.respondWith(c.chat.generate({ prompt: 'hi' }))
})
```

They get `TypeError: fetch is not a function` inside our SDK because we conditionally `import('undici')` in Node-only path but then assume `globalThis.fetch` exists elsewhere. Workers has global fetch but bundlers sometimes rewrite code.

sam: yep. root cause: our bundled SDK includes a small Node-only shim: `const f = globalThis.fetch ?? (await import('undici')).fetch` — but when package is bundled for edge, the bundler hoists/rewrites dynamic import or polyfills incorrectly. Some CJS consumers hit `require('redwood-sdk')` which returns a CommonJS wrapper and `default` shape is different for named exports.

julie: Also saw auth/retry break: in Node undici the `signal` handling differs and our retry wrapper was re-creating requests which lost `Authorization` headers on redirected requests (fetch spec behavior differs with `redirect: 'follow'`). Report from support: auth header lost after 302 -> 200.

sam: checklist suggestion: 1) prefer `globalThis.fetch` when available. 2) fallback to `undici` only in Node where necessary. 3) make `undici` an optional dependency and require users to install it in Node environments that lack global fetch. 4) provide tiny runtime detection helpers that are bundler-safe.

mike: agree. Implementation note: avoid `require('undici')` at top-level. Use dynamic import inside `if (!globalThis.fetch)` and guard for `process?.versions?.node`. Example pattern for Node ESM/CJS compatibility:

```js
// runtime-fetch.js
export async function getFetch() {
  if (typeof globalThis.fetch === 'function') return globalThis.fetch
  // only attempt to load undici in Node
  if (typeof process !== 'undefined' && process.versions && process.versions.node) {
    try {
      const undici = await import('undici')
      return undici.fetch.bind(undici)
    } catch (e) {
      throw new Error('redwood-sdk requires a fetch implementation: please `npm i undici` or provide a global fetch')
    }
  }
  throw new Error('no fetch available in this environment')
}
```

sam: that pattern keeps bundlers from bundling undici into edge builds (because import is guarded at runtime). For CJS consumers: in our build step ensure both ESM and CJS exports are consistent and document `import RedwoodClient from 'redwood-sdk'` vs `const { RedwoodClient } = require('redwood-sdk')` cases.

ana: on types: TS users reported `RedwoodClient` type showing as `any` after transpile when using `esModuleInterop: false`. We should provide both `exports` + `module.exports` patterns and ship .d.ts that work for CJS consumers. Also include `types` in package.json.

julie: also call out edge runtimes that redefine fetch signature (Cloudflare adds `fetch(req, env, ctx)` in Workers — our wrapper should accept same args or forward appropriately).

sam: good point — we'll normalize the wrapper to accept either `(input, init)` or `(event)` and internally convert. But keep narrow surface: we only need `(input, init)` for REST calls. Worker handler support is for example apps.

mike: about retry + auth: ensure our retry replays body safely. For streams you can't clone after consumed — so either buffer small bodies or require the user to supply `buffered: true` for retries. And ensure `credentials: 'include'` vs Authorization header are respected on redirects — add explicit tests that a 302 doesn't drop headers for our code path (we might need to set `redirect: 'manual'` + follow logic that reinserts headers).

sam: action items:
- sam: draft a `runtime-fetch` helper (ESM export) with runtime guards and tests for Node/Cloudflare/edge bundlers.
- ana: update package.json exports & types, add guidance snippet for CJS vs ESM usage in README.
- julie: add e2e test in CI matrix for Cloudflare Workers and a Node 18 minimal with undici installed.
- mike: write tests for redirect + auth header preserving and retry replays.

ana: tiny UX suggestion for onboarding: add a brief "If you're on an edge runtime (Cloudflare/Vercel Edge), DO NOT install undici; if you're on Node <18, install undici" in quickstart. Users kept hitting that.

sam: +1. Also add a troubleshooting FAQ entry: "SDK says fetch missing" with the runtime detection snippet and `npm i undici` note.

ci-bot: pipeline status: a branch `sdk/fetch-fallback` was created, CI will run Workers E2E after tests.

ana: thanks. I'll jump on the README patch and types. Ping me if you need a quick types review. :memo: :rocket:

sam: assigning myself to the runtime helper. Will open draft PR today with tests and a short migration blurb.

mike: I'll own the redirect/retry tests.

julie: I'll add Workers to CI matrix.

ana: closing loop — please add small changelog note for SDK 0.x about fetch behavior and undici optional peer dep.

sam: will do.

ana: resolved for now, moving to threads that need follow-ups. :white_check_mark:
